claim: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 3×10⁸ metres per second.
An electron has a rest mass of approximately 9.11×10⁻³¹ kilograms.
The gravitational acceleration at Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².
Planck's constant has a value of approximately 6.626×10⁻³⁴ joule-seconds.
The wavelength of visible light ranges from approximately 380 nm to 740 nm.
Water has a molecular formula of H₂O and a molar mass of approximately 18 g/mol.
The pH of a neutral aqueous solution at 25°C is 7.0.
Carbon-12 is the most abundant stable isotope of carbon.
The Avogadro constant is approximately 6.022×10²³ per mole.
Sodium chloride (NaCl) dissociates completely into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions when dissolved in water.
Human DNA contains approximately 3 billion base pairs.
The mitochondrion is the primary site of ATP synthesis via oxidative phosphorylation in eukaryotic cells.
DNA replication is semi-conservative: each daughter strand retains one original parental strand.
The human body has 23 pairs of chromosomes, totalling 46.
Photosynthesis in plants occurs in the chloroplast and converts CO₂ and water into glucose using light energy.
A ribosome is approximately 25 nm in diameter.
Enzymes are not used up or permanently altered during the biochemical reactions they catalyse.
The central dogma of molecular biology states that protein sequences cannot be used to determine DNA sequences.
Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928.
Type 1 diabetes is caused by autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreatic islets of Langerhans.
Hypertension is defined as a sustained systolic blood pressure of ≥140 mmHg or diastolic ≥90 mmHg.
The ABO blood group system involves antigens on red blood cell surfaces and corresponding antibodies in plasma.
Statins reduce cardiovascular risk primarily by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol synthesis.
A typical CT scan radiation dose is approximately 10 millisieverts.
HIV antiretroviral therapy suppresses viral replication; it was approved for use in 1987 and includes the drug azidothymidine (AZT).
The sum of the interior angles of any triangle in Euclidean geometry is exactly 180 degrees.
The number π is irrational and cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers.
Euler's identity states that e^(iπ) + 1 = 0.
There are infinitely many prime numbers, as proved by Euclid.
The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.
